newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries gain in London, home sales may be threat.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries gain in London, home sales may be threat.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were pushed higher in London trade, with much of the activity centred on the 10-year sector, traders said.
However, analysts said the recent strong run has left the market vulnerable to any shocks -- and that could be in the form of new home sales data later this session.
"Most of the flow this morning was in the 10-year," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London. "There was also a bit of profit taking, but the pullbacks are being met with buying."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was trading at 103-10, yielding 6.37 percent, at 0920 GMT, compared with 103-06 in Tokyo and 103-04 in New York.
The 10-year notes were trading around 103-28, yielding 6.09 percent after closing around 103-25 in New York.
Traders said there were also sellers of the five-year earlier in the session.
Ian Morris, international economist at HSBC James Capel in London, said June new home sales, due for release at 1400 GMT, could threaten the recent strength in the market.
A Reuters poll showed the figures were expected to stand at 818,000, compared with a previous figure of 825,000.
"Cyclically, anything in the 800,000 area is very high," said Morris. "It's a very volatile series and has produced some upside surprises in the past."
A high number, he said, could set the market tone for the rest of the week. Real GDP for the second quarter is due on Thursday, and the key non-farm payrolls report on Friday.

Morris said the data may show the second quarter economic slowdown is coming to an end, and that more strength is expected in the third quarter. He said he expected the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in September or November.
The U.S. federal funds rate currently stands at 5.50 percent, following a quarter point rise in March.
September T-bond futures were up 2/32 at 116-00. At the short end December Eurodollars were up 0.01 at 94.165.
